faq.q1: Is it safe to run an audit on my site?
faq.a1: Yes. SiteAudit only requests public pages, the same way a search engine does. It respects robots.txt, waits between requests and never submits forms, tries passwords or sends attack payloads.
faq.q2: Can I audit a website I don't own?
faq.a2: You can audit any public website, for example a competitor or a prospective client. The audit only reads publicly available pages and headers. Please use it responsibly and in line with our terms.
faq.a3: Each failed check deducts a fixed number of points depending on its severity and on how many pages it affects. The method is published on the Methodology page. No AI is involved in scoring.
faq.a4: Issue detection and scoring are deterministic rules. Where enabled, an AI model only rewrites the results into a short plain-language summary. Audits work fully without it.
faq.q5: Why does my score differ from other tools?
faq.a5: Tools check different things and weigh them differently. SiteAudit measures from our servers and analyses your HTML and headers; it does not simulate a browser, so it does not report lab metrics such as Largest Contentful Paint.
faq.a6: Up to 10 pages on the free plan, 100 on Pro and 500 on Agency, starting from the address you enter and following internal links and your sitemap.
faq.a7: We store your account and the results of your audits so you can review them later. You can delete any audit, or your whole account, at any time from the app.
faq.q8: Will the audit slow down my website?
faq.a8: No. Requests are made one at a time with a pause between them, and we follow any Crawl-delay you set in robots.txt.

method.title: Methodology
method.meta_description: How SiteAudit collects data, which checks it runs and exactly how scores are calculated.
method.lead: What we measure, how we score it, and what an automated audit cannot tell you.
method.collect_text: SiteAudit requests your pages from our servers, like a search engine crawler. It reads the HTML, the HTTP response headers, robots.txt and the XML sitemap, and checks the links and assets it finds. It does not run JavaScript or render pages in a browser.
method.collect_1: The crawl starts at the address you enter and follows internal links and sitemap entries, up to your plan's page limit and a maximum depth.
method.collect_2: robots.txt rules and Crawl-delay are respected. Requests are sent one at a time with a pause between them.
method.collect_3: Up to 60 linked URLs and 20 assets (stylesheets, scripts, images) from the home page are verified.
method.collect_4: Only public pages are requested. No forms are submitted and no login is attempted.
method.score_text: Each category starts at 100. Every check that fails deducts points once, according to its severity. Checks that run on every page deduct more when they affect more of the audited pages. The overall score is a weighted average of the category scores. Scoring is deterministic and does not use AI.
method.score_site_rules: Site-wide checks (for example security headers or robots.txt) deduct their full weight. A category in which no check could run is shown as not scored and is left out of the overall score.
method.weights_category: Category weights in the overall score
method.limit_1: Response times are measured from our servers and include network distance. They are not browser metrics such as Largest Contentful Paint.
method.limit_2: Content created by JavaScript after the page loads is not analysed.
method.limit_3: Colour contrast is only computed where both colours are set inline; layout overflow and tap-target sizes require a browser and are reported as not determined.
method.limit_4: An automated audit complements, but does not replace, manual review and testing with real users, including users of assistive technology.
method.ai_text: When enabled, an AI model may rewrite the findings into a short plain-language summary. It never detects issues, changes severities or affects scores, and audits work fully without it.
method.rules_text: The complete list of checks, grouped by category.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: What we collect, why, and how long we keep it.
privacy.p1: Account data: your e-mail address, an optional name, your language preference and a salted hash of your password (never the password itself). Usage data: the websites you audit, the audit results, and when audits and report exports happen. Security data: login attempts, with your e-mail address stored only as a keyed hash, and IP addresses, kept for up to two days to prevent abuse.
privacy.p2: To provide the service: run audits, show you your results, enforce plan limits, keep accounts secure and send password-reset e-mails.
privacy.p3: Audits only read publicly available pages and response headers. We store the findings, page addresses and page titles needed to show your results; we do not store the full content of the pages.
privacy.p4: On the free plan, audits are deleted after 30 days. You can delete any audit, or your whole account and all associated data, at any time from Settings.
privacy.p5: We use only strictly necessary cookies: one to keep you signed in, one to protect forms against cross-site request forgery and one to remember your language. No advertising or tracking cookies.
privacy.p6: We do not sell your data. If AI summaries are enabled, a list of findings (not your account data) may be sent to the configured AI provider to generate the summary.
privacy.contact: For questions or requests about your data, contact

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.p1: SiteAudit analyses publicly accessible websites and reports technical findings. Results are automated, informational and provided without guarantee of completeness.
terms.p2: Use SiteAudit only for legitimate purposes. Do not use it to overload websites, to circumvent access restrictions or in breach of any law. We may suspend accounts that abuse the service.
terms.p3: Keep your password confidential. You are responsible for activity under your account.
terms.p4: Each plan includes limits on audits, pages and concurrent audits. Limits may be enforced automatically.
terms.p5: Audit results are recommendations. Decisions about changes to your website remain yours. To the extent permitted by law, we are not liable for indirect losses arising from use of the service.
terms.p6: We may update these terms. Material changes will be announced in the application before they take effect.

title_missing.title: Page has no title
title_missing.description: The page has no <title> element, or it is empty.
title_missing.impact: Search engines show the title as the headline of your result. Without one, they invent a title and your listing is less likely to be clicked.
title_missing.recommendation: Add a unique, descriptive <title> of 15–60 characters that names the page's topic and your brand.

title_length.title: Title is too short or too long
title_length.description: The page title falls outside the recommended length.
title_length.impact: Long titles are cut off in search results; very short titles waste the most visible part of your listing.
title_length.recommendation: Keep titles between 15 and 60 characters, with the most important words first.

title_multiple.title: Page has several title elements
title_multiple.description: More than one <title> element was found.
title_multiple.impact: Search engines will use only one, and which one is not guaranteed.
title_multiple.recommendation: Keep a single <title> in the <head> and remove the others.

description_missing.title: Meta description is missing
description_missing.description: The page has no meta description.
description_missing.impact: Search engines will pick a snippet of page text for your result, which is often less persuasive.
description_missing.recommendation: Write a unique meta description of 70–160 characters that summarises the page and gives a reason to click.

description_length.title: Meta description is too short or too long
description_length.description: The meta description falls outside the recommended length.
description_length.impact: Long descriptions are truncated; short ones miss the chance to persuade.

h1_missing.title: Page has no H1 heading
h1_missing.impact: The main heading tells readers and search engines what the page is about.
h1_missing.recommendation: Add one <h1> that states the page's main topic.

h1_multiple.title: Page has several H1 headings
h1_multiple.description: More than one <h1> heading was found.
h1_multiple.impact: Several top-level headings dilute the page's main topic and make the outline harder to follow.
h1_multiple.recommendation: Use one <h1> for the main topic and <h2>–<h6> for sections.

canonical_missing.title: No canonical URL
canonical_missing.description: The page does not declare a canonical URL.
canonical_missing.impact: When the same content is reachable at several addresses, search engines may split ranking signals between them.
canonical_missing.recommendation: Add <link rel="canonical" href="…"> pointing to the preferred address of the page.

canonical_conflict.title: Conflicting canonical URLs
canonical_conflict.description: The page declares more than one different canonical URL.
canonical_conflict.impact: Search engines ignore conflicting canonicals, so duplicate pages are not consolidated.
canonical_conflict.recommendation: Keep exactly one canonical link per page.

canonical_other_site.title: Canonical points to another website
canonical_other_site.description: The canonical URL is on a different domain.
canonical_other_site.impact: Search engines may drop this page from results in favour of the other site.
canonical_other_site.recommendation: Unless the content intentionally belongs to the other site, point the canonical to this page.

noindex.title: Page is excluded from search results
noindex.description: The page asks search engines not to index it (noindex).
noindex.impact: The page will not appear in search results. This is fine for private or utility pages, but not for content you want found.
noindex.recommendation: Remove noindex from pages that should be found in search.

noindex_home.title: Home page is excluded from search results
noindex_home.description: The home page tells search engines not to index it.
noindex_home.impact: Your home page will disappear from search results, usually taking most of your search traffic with it.
noindex_home.recommendation: Remove the noindex directive from the robots meta tag or the X-Robots-Tag header.

thin_content.title: Little text content
thin_content.description: The page has very little readable text.
thin_content.impact: Pages with little content rarely rank and give visitors few reasons to stay.
thin_content.recommendation: Make sure important pages explain their topic in enough detail. Ignore this for pages that are intentionally short.

generic_anchor.title: Links with vague text
generic_anchor.description: Some links use text such as “click here” or “read more”.
generic_anchor.impact: Link text tells search engines and screen-reader users where a link goes. Vague text says nothing.
generic_anchor.recommendation: Describe the destination in the link text, e.g. “Download the 2024 price list”.

duplicate_title.title: Same title used on several pages
duplicate_title.description: Several pages share the same title.
duplicate_title.impact: Search engines struggle to tell the pages apart and may show the wrong one.
duplicate_title.recommendation: Give every page a unique title.

duplicate_description.title: Same meta description on several pages
duplicate_description.description: Several pages share the same meta description.
duplicate_description.impact: Duplicate descriptions make results look identical and are often ignored by search engines.
duplicate_description.recommendation: Write a specific description for each important page.

duplicate_content.title: Duplicate page content
duplicate_content.description: Pages with identical text were found at different addresses.
duplicate_content.impact: Search engines may index the wrong version or split ranking signals between copies.
duplicate_content.recommendation: Redirect duplicates to one address or set a canonical URL.

robots_missing.title: No robots.txt file
robots_missing.description: The site has no robots.txt file.
robots_missing.impact: Not harmful on its own, but robots.txt is where you point crawlers to your sitemap and keep them out of areas that should not be crawled.
robots_missing.recommendation: Add a robots.txt at the site root with at least a Sitemap line.

robots_blocks_all.title: robots.txt blocks search engines
robots_blocks_all.description: robots.txt disallows the whole site for search engine crawlers.
robots_blocks_all.impact: Search engines will stop crawling your pages and they will drop out of results.
robots_blocks_all.recommendation: Remove “Disallow: /” for search engines unless the site is intentionally private.

sitemap_missing.title: No XML sitemap found
sitemap_missing.description: No sitemap was found in robots.txt or at /sitemap.xml.
sitemap_missing.impact: Sitemaps help search engines discover all your pages, especially new or deeply linked ones.
sitemap_missing.recommendation: Publish an XML sitemap and reference it in robots.txt.

sitemap_invalid.title: Sitemap is not valid XML
sitemap_invalid.description: The sitemap could not be read as a valid XML sitemap.
sitemap_invalid.impact: Search engines cannot use a sitemap they cannot parse.
sitemap_invalid.recommendation: Fix the XML so it follows the sitemaps.org format.

broken_internal_links.title: Broken internal links
broken_internal_links.description: Links point to pages on your site that return an error or cannot be reached.
broken_internal_links.impact: Visitors hit dead ends and search engines waste crawl budget on missing pages.
broken_internal_links.recommendation: Update or remove the links, or redirect the missing pages to their replacements.

internal_redirects.title: Internal links that redirect
internal_redirects.description: Some internal links point to an address that redirects elsewhere.
internal_redirects.impact: Each redirect adds a round trip for visitors and crawlers.
internal_redirects.recommendation: Link directly to the final address.

open_graph_missing.title: Open Graph tags missing
open_graph_missing.description: The home page is missing Open Graph tags used for link previews.
open_graph_missing.impact: Links shared on social networks and messaging apps show without a proper title, description or image.
open_graph_missing.recommendation: Add og:title, og:description and og:image to the home page and key pages.

structured_data_missing.title: No structured data
structured_data_missing.description: No JSON-LD structured data was found on the audited pages.
structured_data_missing.impact: Structured data can make your results eligible for richer search features.
structured_data_missing.recommendation: Consider adding schema.org markup appropriate for your content, e.g. Organization or Product.

https_canonical_mismatch.title: Canonical uses http:// on an HTTPS site
https_canonical_mismatch.description: The site is served over HTTPS but the canonical URL uses http://.
https_canonical_mismatch.impact: Search engines receive mixed signals about which version to index.

response_very_slow.title: Very slow server response
response_very_slow.description: The server took a long time to send the page.
response_very_slow.impact: Visitors wait before anything appears and many leave. Slow responses also reduce how much of your site search engines crawl.
response_very_slow.recommendation: Look at server-side caching, database queries and hosting capacity, or put a CDN in front of the site.

response_slow.title: Slow server response
response_slow.description: The server was slower than recommended to send the page.
response_slow.impact: Every visit starts with this delay.
response_slow.recommendation: Enable page caching and check server performance.

html_large.title: Very large HTML document
html_large.description: The page's HTML is unusually large.
html_large.impact: Large documents take longer to download and parse, especially on mobile networks.
html_large.recommendation: Remove inlined data and unused markup; paginate long lists.

html_uncompressed.title: HTML is not compressed
html_uncompressed.description: The server sends HTML without gzip or Brotli compression.
html_uncompressed.impact: Compression typically reduces HTML size by 70% or more.
html_uncompressed.recommendation: Enable gzip or Brotli compression on the web server or CDN.

render_blocking_scripts.title: Render-blocking scripts
render_blocking_scripts.description: Scripts in the <head> load without async or defer.
render_blocking_scripts.impact: The browser stops drawing the page until each script has downloaded and run.
render_blocking_scripts.recommendation: Add defer (or async for independent scripts), or move scripts to the end of <body>.

many_stylesheets.title: Many render-blocking stylesheets
many_stylesheets.description: The page loads more than five stylesheets in the <head>.
many_stylesheets.impact: Each stylesheet must download before the page is displayed.
many_stylesheets.recommendation: Combine stylesheets and inline the critical CSS.

images_without_dimensions.title: Images without width and height
images_without_dimensions.description: Images do not declare their dimensions.
images_without_dimensions.impact: The layout jumps as images load (layout shift), which is distracting and can cause mis-clicks.
images_without_dimensions.recommendation: Set width and height attributes on images, or reserve space with CSS aspect-ratio.

no_lazy_loading.title: No lazy loading for images
no_lazy_loading.description: The page has many images and none use lazy loading.
no_lazy_loading.impact: Images below the fold are downloaded up front, competing with what the visitor sees first.
no_lazy_loading.recommendation: Add loading="lazy" to images that are not visible on the first screen.

large_inline_code.title: Large inline scripts or styles
large_inline_code.description: The HTML contains a large amount of inline JavaScript or CSS.
large_inline_code.impact: Inline code cannot be cached separately and is re-downloaded on every page.
large_inline_code.recommendation: Move large inline code to external, cacheable files.

many_requests.title: Many resources on the home page
many_requests.description: The home page references a large number of scripts, stylesheets and images.
many_requests.impact: Every resource costs a request; many requests slow down the page, especially on mobile.
many_requests.recommendation: Remove unused resources, combine files and lazy-load images.

entry_redirects.title: Redirect chain on the entry URL
entry_redirects.description: Reaching the home page takes several redirects.
entry_redirects.impact: Each hop adds a full round trip before the page starts loading.
entry_redirects.recommendation: Redirect directly to the final address in a single step.

static_not_cached.title: Assets without long-term caching
static_not_cached.description: Stylesheets, scripts or images are served without a long cache lifetime.
static_not_cached.impact: Returning visitors download the same files again.
static_not_cached.recommendation: Serve versioned static files with Cache-Control: max-age of at least a week (ideally a year, with immutable).

text_resources_uncompressed.title: Uncompressed CSS or JavaScript
text_resources_uncompressed.description: Text assets are served without compression.
text_resources_uncompressed.impact: CSS and JavaScript typically shrink by 60–80% with compression.
text_resources_uncompressed.recommendation: Enable gzip or Brotli for CSS, JavaScript, SVG and JSON.

large_images.title: Large images
large_images.description: Some images are larger than recommended.
large_images.impact: Heavy images are the most common cause of slow pages on mobile.
large_images.recommendation: Resize images to the size they are displayed at and use modern formats such as WebP or AVIF.

heavy_javascript.title: Heavy JavaScript
heavy_javascript.description: The home page loads a large amount of JavaScript.
heavy_javascript.impact: JavaScript must be downloaded, parsed and executed, which delays interactivity on slower devices.
heavy_javascript.recommendation: Remove unused libraries, split code by page and defer non-essential scripts.

fonts_without_preconnect.title: Web fonts without preconnect
fonts_without_preconnect.description: Google Fonts are used without a preconnect hint.
fonts_without_preconnect.impact: Text may render late while the browser connects to the font servers.
fonts_without_preconnect.recommendation: Add <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>, or self-host the fonts.

lang_missing.title: Page language not declared
lang_missing.description: The <html> element has no lang attribute.
lang_missing.impact: Screen readers may pronounce the content in the wrong language. (WCAG 3.1.1)

image_alt_missing.title: Images without alternative text
image_alt_missing.impact: Screen-reader users get no description of the image, or hear the file name. (WCAG 1.1.1)
image_alt_missing.recommendation: Add alt text describing each informative image; use alt="" for purely decorative images.

control_unlabeled.title: Form fields without labels
control_unlabeled.description: Form fields have no associated label.
control_unlabeled.impact: Screen-reader users cannot tell what to enter. Placeholders disappear while typing and are not a substitute. (WCAG 1.3.1, 4.1.2)
control_unlabeled.recommendation: Connect a <label for="…"> to every field, or use aria-label when a visible label is not possible.

button_unnamed.title: Buttons without an accessible name
button_unnamed.description: Buttons have no text, label or title.
button_unnamed.impact: Assistive technology announces them only as “button”, so users cannot tell what they do. (WCAG 4.1.2)
button_unnamed.recommendation: Give every button visible text, or an aria-label for icon-only buttons.

link_unnamed.title: Links without an accessible name
link_unnamed.description: Links have no text, label or image alternative.
link_unnamed.impact: Screen-reader users hear only the address, or nothing. (WCAG 2.4.4)
link_unnamed.recommendation: Add link text, or alt text to the image inside the link.

iframe_untitled.title: Frames without a title
iframe_untitled.impact: Users of assistive technology cannot tell what the embedded content is. (WCAG 4.1.2)
iframe_untitled.recommendation: Add a short title, e.g. title="Location map".

invalid_role.title: Invalid ARIA roles
invalid_role.description: Elements use role values that do not exist in ARIA.
invalid_role.impact: Assistive technology ignores or misinterprets the element.
invalid_role.recommendation: Use valid ARIA roles, or preferably the native HTML element.

duplicate_ids.title: Duplicate element IDs
duplicate_ids.description: Several elements share the same id.
duplicate_ids.impact: Labels, ARIA references and in-page links may point to the wrong element.
duplicate_ids.recommendation: Make every id unique within the page.

positive_tabindex.title: Positive tabindex values
positive_tabindex.impact: Keyboard focus jumps in an unexpected order. (WCAG 2.4.3)
positive_tabindex.recommendation: Use tabindex="0" or -1 only, and order elements correctly in the HTML.

heading_order.title: Heading levels are skipped
heading_order.description: Headings jump more than one level (for example from H2 to H4).
heading_order.impact: Screen-reader users navigate by headings; skipped levels suggest missing sections.
heading_order.recommendation: Use heading levels in order, without gaps.

empty_heading.title: Empty headings
empty_heading.impact: Screen readers announce a heading with nothing in it.
empty_heading.recommendation: Add text to the heading or remove the element.

main_landmark_missing.title: No main landmark
main_landmark_missing.description: The page has no <main> element or role="main".
main_landmark_missing.impact: Keyboard and screen-reader users cannot jump straight to the main content.
main_landmark_missing.recommendation: Wrap the primary content in a <main> element.

table_headers_missing.title: Data tables without headers
table_headers_missing.description: Tables have several rows but no header cells.
table_headers_missing.impact: Screen readers cannot tell which column or row a value belongs to. (WCAG 1.3.1)
table_headers_missing.recommendation: Use <th> for header cells, or role="presentation" for layout tables.

zoom_disabled.title: Zoom is disabled
zoom_disabled.description: The viewport prevents users from zooming in.
zoom_disabled.impact: People with low vision cannot enlarge the text. (WCAG 1.4.4)
zoom_disabled.recommendation: Remove user-scalable=no and any maximum-scale below 2 from the viewport tag.

low_contrast.title: Low colour contrast
low_contrast.description: Text colours set inline have insufficient contrast with their background.
low_contrast.impact: Text is hard to read for people with low vision or in bright light. (WCAG 1.4.3 requires 4.5:1)
low_contrast.recommendation: Darken the text or lighten the background to reach at least 4.5:1.

contrast_stylesheets.title: Colour contrast of styled text
contrast_stylesheets.description: Contrast of colours defined in stylesheets.
contrast_stylesheets.recommendation: Check contrast with a browser-based tool.

viewport_missing.title: No mobile viewport
viewport_missing.description: The page has no viewport meta tag.
viewport_missing.impact: Phones render the page at desktop width and shrink it, so text is tiny and users must zoom.

viewport_fixed_width.title: Viewport has a fixed width
viewport_fixed_width.description: The viewport is set to a fixed pixel width instead of the device width.
viewport_fixed_width.impact: The layout does not adapt to the screen size of the phone.

plugins.title: Embedded plugins
plugins.impact: Plugin content does not work on most mobile devices.
plugins.recommendation: Replace plugin content with HTML5 video, audio or images.

wide_fixed_elements.title: Wide fixed-width elements
wide_fixed_elements.description: Elements have inline widths larger than a phone screen.
wide_fixed_elements.impact: They may force horizontal scrolling on small screens.
wide_fixed_elements.recommendation: Use relative widths (%, max-width: 100%) instead of fixed pixel widths.

small_inline_fonts.title: Very small text
small_inline_fonts.description: Text is set inline to a font size below 12 px.
small_inline_fonts.impact: Small text is hard to read on phones.
small_inline_fonts.recommendation: Use at least 16 px for body text and 12 px for fine print.

images_not_responsive.title: Images are not responsive
images_not_responsive.description: None of the page's images provide alternative sizes (srcset or <picture>).
images_not_responsive.recommendation: Provide srcset and sizes so browsers can pick an appropriate size.

layout_overflow.title: Horizontal overflow on small screens
layout_overflow.recommendation: Check the page on a phone or with browser developer tools.

tap_targets.title: Size of tap targets
tap_targets.description: Whether buttons and links are large enough to tap.
tap_targets.recommendation: Check that interactive elements are at least 24×24 px (WCAG 2.5.8).

no_https.title: Site is not served over HTTPS
no_https.description: The site is delivered over unencrypted HTTP.
no_https.impact: Anyone on the network can read or alter what visitors see and send. Browsers mark the site as “Not secure”.
no_https.recommendation: Install a TLS certificate (free from Let's Encrypt) and redirect all HTTP traffic to HTTPS.

http_not_redirected.title: HTTP does not redirect to HTTPS
http_not_redirected.description: The http:// version of the site does not redirect to https://.
http_not_redirected.impact: Visitors who type the address or follow old links stay on an unencrypted connection.
http_not_redirected.recommendation: Add a permanent (301) redirect from HTTP to HTTPS.

certificate_invalid.title: TLS certificate is not valid
certificate_invalid.description: The certificate could not be verified.
certificate_invalid.impact: Browsers show a full-page security warning and most visitors leave.
certificate_invalid.recommendation: Install a valid certificate for this host name, including the full intermediate chain.

certificate_expiring.title: TLS certificate expires soon
certificate_expiring.impact: When it expires, browsers will block access to the site with a security warning.
certificate_expiring.recommendation: Renew the certificate and make sure renewal is automated.

hsts_missing.title: HSTS header missing
hsts_missing.description: The Strict-Transport-Security header is not set.
hsts_missing.impact: Browsers may still try plain HTTP first, which can be intercepted.
hsts_missing.recommendation: Send Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains once HTTPS works everywhere.

csp_missing.title: No Content Security Policy
csp_missing.description: The Content-Security-Policy header is not set.
csp_missing.impact: A CSP limits the damage of cross-site scripting by restricting where scripts can load from.
csp_missing.recommendation: Define a Content-Security-Policy, starting in report-only mode to find what needs to be allowed.

clickjacking.title: Page can be embedded by other sites
clickjacking.description: Neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors is set.
clickjacking.impact: Attackers can load your page in an invisible frame and trick users into clicking (clickjacking).
clickjacking.recommendation: Send X-Frame-Options: DENY (or SAMEORIGIN), or CSP frame-ancestors 'self'.

nosniff_missing.title: X-Content-Type-Options missing
nosniff_missing.description: The X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header is not set.
nosniff_missing.impact: Browsers may guess content types, which can turn uploaded files into executable scripts.

referrer_policy_missing.title: Referrer-Policy missing
referrer_policy_missing.impact: Full page addresses, which may contain private data, can leak to other sites.

permissions_policy_missing.title: Permissions-Policy missing
permissions_policy_missing.impact: Embedded third-party content could request features such as camera or location.
permissions_policy_missing.recommendation: Send a Permissions-Policy that disables features you do not use, e.g. camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=().

cookie_not_secure.title: Cookies without the Secure flag
cookie_not_secure.description: Cookies are set without the Secure attribute.
cookie_not_secure.impact: They can be sent over unencrypted connections and intercepted.
cookie_not_secure.recommendation: Set the Secure attribute on all cookies.

cookie_not_httponly.title: Cookies readable by JavaScript
cookie_not_httponly.description: Cookies are set without the HttpOnly attribute.
cookie_not_httponly.impact: If a session cookie is readable by JavaScript, a cross-site scripting flaw can steal it. Analytics cookies do not need HttpOnly.
cookie_not_httponly.recommendation: Set HttpOnly on session and authentication cookies.

cookie_no_samesite.title: Cookies without SameSite
cookie_no_samesite.description: Cookies are set without the SameSite attribute.
cookie_no_samesite.impact: Without SameSite, cookies are more exposed to cross-site request forgery.

mixed_content.title: Mixed content
mixed_content.description: An HTTPS page loads resources over plain HTTP.
mixed_content.impact: Browsers block or warn about insecure resources, which can break the page and expose visitors.

version_disclosure.title: Server software version disclosed
version_disclosure.description: Response headers reveal software names and versions.
version_disclosure.impact: Version numbers make it easier for attackers to find known vulnerabilities.
version_disclosure.recommendation: Remove version numbers from the Server header and remove X-Powered-By.

doctype_missing.title: No HTML doctype
doctype_missing.description: The page does not start with <!doctype html>.
doctype_missing.impact: Browsers render the page in quirks mode, which causes inconsistent layout.

charset_missing.title: Character encoding not declared
charset_missing.description: Neither the HTML nor the Content-Type header declares a character set.
charset_missing.recommendation: Add <meta charset="utf-8"> as the first element of <head>.

deprecated_html.title: Deprecated HTML elements
deprecated_html.description: The page uses elements removed from HTML.
deprecated_html.impact: They may render inconsistently and signal outdated markup.
deprecated_html.recommendation: Replace them with CSS and current HTML elements.

meta_refresh.title: Meta refresh used
meta_refresh.description: The page uses a meta refresh to reload or redirect.
meta_refresh.impact: Automatic refreshes disorient users and are a weak redirect signal for search engines.

target_blank.title: External links opening new tabs without rel=noopener
target_blank.description: Links with target="_blank" do not set rel="noopener".
target_blank.impact: Current browsers apply noopener automatically; older browsers let the opened page control yours.
target_blank.recommendation: Add rel="noopener" to links that open in a new tab.

favicon_missing.title: No favicon declared
favicon_missing.description: The home page does not declare a favicon.
favicon_missing.impact: Browser tabs, bookmarks and some search results show a generic icon.

server_errors.title: Pages return server errors
server_errors.description: Some pages respond with a 5xx server error.
server_errors.impact: Visitors see an error page and search engines may drop the page.
server_errors.recommendation: Check the server logs for these addresses and fix the underlying errors.

unreachable_pages.title: Pages could not be reached
unreachable_pages.description: Some linked pages could not be fetched.
unreachable_pages.impact: Visitors and search engines cannot reach these pages either.
unreachable_pages.recommendation: Check that these pages are online and respond within a few seconds.

broken_external_links.title: Broken outbound links
broken_external_links.description: Links to other websites point to pages that no longer exist or do not respond.
broken_external_links.impact: Dead links frustrate visitors and make content look neglected.
